questions.question: The observable physical and physiological characteristics of an organism resulting from its genetic makeup and environmental interactions are termed its: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: The phenotype refers to the expressed, observable physical traits, biochemical properties, and behaviors of an organism (such as tall height or brown eye color), determined by its underlying genotype.

questions.question: When an organism carries two identical alleles for a specific gene (e.g., TT or tt), its genetic condition is described as: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Homozygous describes an individual carrying two identical alleles for a particular locus on homologous chromosomes (homozygous dominant TT or homozygous recessive tt).

questions.question: In a classical Mendelian monohybrid cross, what is the expected phenotypic ratio among offspring in the F2 generation? (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: When heterozygous F1 individuals (Tt x Tt) are crossed, the resulting F2 generation yields a 3:1 phenotypic ratio (3 displaying the dominant trait to 1 displaying the recessive trait) and a 1:2:1 genotypic ratio.

questions.question: In a Mendelian dihybrid cross involving two independently assorting traits (e.g., RrYy x RrYy), what is the characteristic F2 phenotypic ratio? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: According to Mendels Law of Independent Assortment, a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous parents yields a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a classic genetic example of co-dominance in human biology? (FBISE 2022)

options.B: AB blood group of the ABO blood system

questions.explanation: In human ABO blood groups, alleles IA and IB are co-dominant: both are fully and equally expressed on red blood cell surfaces in heterozygous individuals (IA IB), producing blood type AB.

questions.question: A father has blood group B and his biological child has blood group O. What must be the father genotype?
questions.explanation: A child with blood group O has genotype ii and must receive one recessive i allele from each parent. Therefore, a father with blood group B must carry the heterozygous genotype IB i.

questions.question: When a red-flowered plant is crossed with a white-flowered plant of Mirabilis jalapa (4 oclock plant) and all F1 offspring produce pink flowers, this phenomenon is called: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance, neither allele is completely dominant. The heterozygous phenotype is an intermediate blend between the two homozygous parents, producing pink flowers (Rr) from red (RR) and white (rr).

questions.question: The two complementary anti-parallel polynucleotide strands of a DNA double helix are bonded together by: (FBISE 2024)

options.B: Hydrogen bonds between complementary nitrogenous bases

questions.explanation: The two strands of the DNA double helix are stabilized by hydrogen bonds between complementary base pairs: Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine (A=T), and Guanine forms three with Cytosine (G≡C).

questions.question: According to Chargaff rules of base pairing in double-stranded DNA, adenine always pairs specifically with: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: In double-stranded DNA, the purine Adenine pairs specifically with the pyrimidine Thymine via two hydrogen bonds (A=T), while Guanine pairs with Cytosine (G≡C).

questions.question: A specific sequence of nucleotide bases along a DNA molecule that encodes instructions for synthesizing a functional polypeptide chain is defined as a:
questions.explanation: A gene is the fundamental physical and functional unit of heredity, consisting of a distinct sequence of DNA nucleotides that determines the amino acid sequence of a protein.

questions.question: The specific physical position or address occupied by a gene along the length of a chromosome is termed its: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: The locus (plural: loci) is the fixed anatomical position on a chromosome where a particular gene or genetic marker is located.

questions.question: Alternate structural forms of the same gene that occupy identical loci on homologous chromosomes are called: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Alleles are variant versions of a given gene that govern the same trait (e.g., T for tall and t for dwarf) situated at corresponding positions on homologous chromosomes.

questions.question: Why did Gregor Johann Mendel specifically select the garden pea plant (Pisum sativum) for his historic hybridization experiments? (FBISE 2024)

options.A: It took several decades to reproduce one generation
options.B: It possessed distinct, sharply contrasting traits and could be easily cross-pollinated
options.C: It had over 500 chromosomes per cell

questions.explanation: Mendel chose Pisum sativum because it has distinct contrasting traits (e.g., tall vs dwarf, yellow vs green seeds), short generation time, high fecundity, and natural self-pollination that can be controlled.

questions.question: Mendel Law of Segregation states that during the biological process of gamete formation (meiosis): (FBISE 2023)

options.A: All chromosomes fuse into a single diploid nucleus
options.B: The two alleles of each gene pair separate so that each gamete carries only one allele
options.C: Alleles blend together permanently to create a uniform hybrid

questions.explanation: Mendels First Law (Law of Segregation) states that homologous chromosomes and their constituent allele pairs separate during meiosis, ensuring each gamete receives only one allele from each parent.

questions.question: In humans, which of the following physiological traits is an example of continuous phenotypic variation?
questions.explanation: Continuous variations (such as height, weight, and skin color) exhibit a complete bell-shaped spectrum of phenotypes without clear-cut categories, because they are polygenic and influenced by environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is a classic example of discontinuous (discrete) variation in the human population? (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Discontinuous variations fall into distinct, discrete qualitative classes without intermediates (e.g., blood types A, B, AB, O; tongue roller vs non-roller), controlled by a single gene.

questions.question: Eukaryotic chromatin is composed of approximately what ratio of DNA to histone proteins?
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic chromosomes consist of chromatin fibers made of roughly 40% double-stranded DNA coiled around 60% basic nuclear proteins called histones.

questions.question: The fundamental structural repeating unit of chromatin, where 147 base pairs of DNA wind around an octamer of histone proteins, is the: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: A nucleosome is the structural unit consisting of a segment of DNA wound around a core particle composed of eight histone protein molecules (an octamer), resembling beads on a string.

questions.question: Which mechanism during prophase I of meiosis generates new combinations of maternal and paternal alleles on homologous chromosomes?
questions.explanation: During pachynema of prophase I, non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange genetic segments at chiasmata (crossing over), creating novel allele combinations.

questions.question: Who published On the Origin of Species in 1859, formulating the scientific theory of evolution by natural selection? (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection in 1859, proposing that organisms possessing advantageous variations are more likely to survive and reproduce.

questions.question: The intentional breeding of organisms by humans to produce domestic animals and crops with desirable economic traits is termed: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Artificial selection (selective breeding) is the practice of humans choosing specific individual animals or plants with desirable traits (e.g., high milk yield in cattle) to reproduce.

questions.question: An allele whose phenotypic effect is fully masked and unexpressed in the presence of an alternate dominant allele is called: (FBISE 2024)
questions.explanation: A recessive allele is one whose phenotypic expression is suppressed in a heterozygous genotype and is manifested only when present in a homozygous state.

questions.question: If a homozygous tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a homozygous dwarf pea plant (tt), what percentage of the F1 generation will be tall?
questions.explanation: All F1 offspring will receive a dominant T allele from the homozygous tall parent and a recessive t allele from the dwarf parent, yielding 100% heterozygous tall (Tt) plants.

questions.question: The three components of a single DNA nucleotide monomer are:

options.A: A fatty acid, glycerol, and nitrogen base
options.B: A deoxyribose 5-carbon sugar, a phosphate group, and a nitrogenous base
options.C: An amino acid, ribose sugar, and peptide chain

questions.explanation: A DNA nucleotide consists of three covalently bonded units: a five-carbon deoxyribose sugar, a negatively charged phosphate group, and one of four nitrogenous bases (A, T, G, or C).

questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is found in RNA molecules instead of thymine?
questions.explanation: RNA contains Uracil (U) in place of Thymine (T). Uracil forms complementary hydrogen bonds with Adenine during transcription and protein synthesis.

questions.question: In a cross between two heterozygous pink-flowered Mirabilis jalapa plants (Rr x Rr), what phenotypic ratio will be obtained?
questions.explanation: Under incomplete dominance, a self-cross of pink heterozygotes (Rr x Rr) produces 1/4 homozygous red (RR), 2/4 heterozygous pink (Rr), and 1/4 homozygous white (rr), giving a 1:2:1 ratio.

questions.question: What is the primary evolutionary driving force proposed by Charles Darwin that leads to adaptation and speciation?

options.B: Differential reproductive success via natural selection
options.C: Deliberate human intervention in natural habitats

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on heritable variations: individuals best adapted to their local ecological environment survive and reproduce in greater numbers, passing adaptive alleles to offspring.

questions.question: How many total chromosomes are present in a normal, non-dividing human somatic body cell?
questions.explanation: Human diploid (2n) somatic cells contain exactly 46 chromosomes, consisting of 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XX in females, XY in males).

questions.question: A sudden, permanent heritable alteration in the nucleotide sequence of an organism DNA is termed a: (FBISE 2023)
questions.explanation: A mutation is an alteration in the nucleotide sequence of the genome, caused by replication errors or environmental mutagens (radiation, chemicals), providing raw material for evolution.

questions.question: What is the biological term for the entire set of genes present in a complete haploid set of chromosomes in an organism?
questions.explanation: An organisms genome is the complete genetic content or total DNA sequence contained within a single haploid set of chromosomes.

questions.question: Which of the following blood group genotypes will result in blood group A?
questions.explanation: Blood group A is determined either by the homozygous genotype IA IA or the heterozygous genotype IA i, where the IA allele is dominant over the recessive i allele.

questions.question: When both alleles of a gene pair contribute independently and visibly to the phenotype without any blending, the relationship is: (FBISE 2022)
questions.explanation: Co-dominance is the condition where both alleles in a heterozygote are fully and simultaneously expressed without blending, producing a phenotype with both distinct gene products.

questions.question: In peas, round seed shape (R) is dominant over wrinkled seed shape (r). If a heterozygous round plant (Rr) is crossed with a wrinkled plant (rr), what fraction of offspring will be wrinkled?
questions.explanation: This test cross (Rr x rr) yields gametes R and r from the heterozygote and r from the wrinkled parent, producing 50% heterozygous round (Rr) and 50% homozygous wrinkled (rr).

questions.question: The historical French biologist who incorrectly proposed the theory of inheritance of acquired characteristics was: (FBISE 2021)
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed that physical traits acquired by an organism through use or disuse during its lifetime could be passed down directly to its progeny, a hypothesis later disproved.

questions.question: The total collection of all alleles for all genes present in an interbreeding population at a given time is called the:
questions.explanation: The gene pool represents the sum total of all genetic information and alleles carried by all the individuals in a specific interbreeding biological population.
